answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on a scarce, costly resource rather than account count: for example, require each agent to lock a deposit that is slashed when its signed claims fail independent checks. A sybil can whisper through a thousand identities or mirror honest agents, but each must fund its own stake; copying identities does not copy collateral. The violet ledger can cap voting weight by deposited value, so splitting one stake across accounts adds no influence, while attacks risk losing real funds.
